description: Curated Recomposition exercise library. Read-only reference data; ids are permanent and never reused.

exercises.name: Barbell Flat Bench Press
exercises.description: Lie on a bench and press a barbell up from your chest. A core strength lift for the chest, shoulders and triceps.
exercises.notes: A rack or safeties are recommended for heavy sets.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: Press a barbell up from an inclined bench. Emphasizes the upper chest and front delts with heavy loading.
exercises.notes: Upper-chest version of the flat barbell press. Inclines up to about 45 degrees are classified as horizontal-push.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Flat Bench Press
exercises.description: Press dumbbells up from a flat bench. A freer path and deeper stretch than a barbell for the chest, front delts and triceps.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.description: Press dumbbells upward while lying on an inclined bench. Emphasizes the upper chest and front shoulders.
exercises.notes: Inclines up to about 45 degrees are classified as horizontal-push.

exercises.name: Seated Machine Chest Press
exercises.description: Press the handles forward from a seated, back-supported position. A stable, easy-to-load way to train the chest, front delts and triceps.

exercises.name: Incline Machine Chest Press
exercises.description: Press the handles up and forward on an angled machine. Emphasizes the upper chest and front delts with a fixed, stable path.

exercises.name: Incline Smith Machine Press
exercises.description: Press a Smith machine bar up from an inclined bench. A guided path for the upper chest and front delts.

exercises.name: Flat Smith Machine Bench Press
exercises.description: Press a Smith machine bar up from a flat bench. A guided path for the chest, front delts and triceps.

exercises.name: High-to-Low Cable Flye
exercises.description: Sweep the cable handles down and together in front of your lower chest, starting from high pulleys. Isolates the chest, with extra emphasis on the lower fibers.
exercises.notes: Lower-chest emphasis. Cable Crossover is the usual gym name for this version.

exercises.name: Low-to-High Cable Flye
exercises.description: Sweep the cable handles up and together in front of your upper chest, starting from low pulleys. Isolates the upper chest.
exercises.notes: Upper-chest emphasis.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Flye
exercises.description: Sit on a flat bench between the cable stacks and bring the handles together in a wide hugging arc. Isolates the chest.

exercises.name: Pec Deck Flye
exercises.description: Bring the machine handles together in front of your chest from a seated, supported position. Isolates the chest with a stable path.

exercises.name: Weighted Chest Dips
exercises.description: Lower and press your body between parallel bars, leaning forward. Works the lower chest and triceps; add load with a dip belt once bodyweight reps are easy.
exercises.notes: Classified horizontal-push: a forward-lean chest dip is close to a decline press. Bodyweight to start; load is added with a dip belt. The upright, triceps-focused version is its own entry.

exercises.name: Deficit Push-Up
exercises.description: Push-up with your hands raised on handles or plates so your chest sinks below hand level. A deeper stretch for the chest.
exercises.notes: Needs something to raise the hands (push-up handles, plates or blocks); not listed as equipment.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: Pull a neutral-grip handle down to your upper chest while seated. Builds the lats with a shoulder-friendly grip.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: Pull a bar down to your upper chest while seated. Builds the lats and is easy to scale to your strength.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: Pull a single cable handle down toward your side, one arm at a time. Isolates each lat with a full stretch and squeeze.

exercises.name: Weighted Pull-Up
exercises.description: Hang from a bar and pull your chest toward it, adding load with a dip belt as you progress. A key lift for the lats and upper back.
exercises.notes: Done at bodyweight or with added load. A chin-up (palms facing you) is its own entry.

exercises.name: Weighted Chin-Up
exercises.description: Hang from a bar with an underhand grip and pull your chin over it, adding load as you progress. Works the lats with extra biceps involvement.
exercises.notes: The underhand grip shifts more work to the biceps than a pull-up.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported T-Bar Row
exercises.description: Row the handles toward your torso with your chest braced on a pad. Builds the upper back and lats without lower-back strain.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: Lie chest-down on an incline bench and row dumbbells toward your hips. Trains the upper back and rear delts with no momentum.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.description: Sit and row a cable handle toward your torso. Trains the mid-back and lats with steady tension.

exercises.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.description: Hinge forward and row a barbell to your lower ribs. Builds the lats and upper back with heavy loading.

exercises.name: Pendlay Row
exercises.description: Row a barbell from the floor to your lower chest, resetting on the floor each rep. A strict, explosive builder for the back.

exercises.name: Meadows Row
exercises.description: Row the end of a landmine barbell one arm at a time, standing side-on to the bar. Builds the lats and upper back with a long stretch.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: Row a dumbbell to your hip with one hand and knee on a bench. Builds the lats and upper back one side at a time.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Lat Row
exercises.description: Row a single cable handle toward your hip while seated or kneeling at a bench. Isolates each lat with steady tension.

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Cable Pullover
exercises.description: With straight arms, sweep a cable bar down from overhead to your thighs. Isolates the lats through a long range of motion.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Pullover
exercises.description: Lie across a bench and arc a dumbbell from behind your head to above your chest. Stretches the lats, with help from the chest.

exercises.name: Barbell Shrug
exercises.description: Shrug a barbell upward with straight arms, lifting your shoulders toward your ears. Builds the upper traps.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrug
exercises.description: Shrug dumbbells upward at your sides, lifting your shoulders toward your ears. Builds the upper traps with a natural arm path.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Kelso Shrug
exercises.description: Lie chest-down on an incline bench and pull your shoulder blades together and up with dumbbells. Targets the mid traps and rhomboids.
exercises.notes: Scapular retraction, so classified horizontal-pull.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.description: Press dumbbells overhead, seated or standing. Trains the shoulders and triceps with a freer path than a barbell.
exercises.notes: Seated with the bench set upright. Standing is also fine; the bench is the supported setup.

exercises.name: Standing Overhead Barbell Press
exercises.description: Press a barbell from your shoulders to overhead while standing. Builds shoulder strength and upper-body stability.
exercises.notes: Performed standing, pressed from the rack.

exercises.name: Seated Smith Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.description: Press a Smith machine bar overhead from a seated, upright bench. A guided path for the shoulders and triceps.

exercises.name: Seated Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.description: Press the handles overhead from a seated, back-supported position. A stable way to load the shoulders and triceps.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Raise a cable handle out to your side up to shoulder height. The cable keeps constant tension on the side delt.

exercises.name: Behind-the-Back Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Raise a cable handle out to your side with the cable passing behind your back. Loads the side delt hard at the bottom of the lift.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Raise dumbbells out to your sides up to shoulder height. Isolates the side delts.
exercises.notes: Light loads; strict form matters more than weight.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Incline Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Lie chest-down on an incline bench and raise dumbbells out to your sides. Removes momentum so the side delts do the work.

exercises.name: Machine Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Raise the machine pads out to your sides from a seated position. Isolates the side delts with a fixed, stable path.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.description: Face the pad and pull the machine handles back and out in a wide arc. Isolates the rear delts with a stable path.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Rear Delt Flye
exercises.description: Lie chest-down on an incline bench and raise dumbbells out to your sides. Isolates the rear delts without momentum.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Flye
exercises.description: Cross the cable handles and pull them back and out to your sides. Isolates the rear delts with constant tension.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Face Pull
exercises.description: Pull a rope toward your face with your elbows high. Targets the rear delts and upper back and supports shoulder health.
exercises.notes: A shoulder-health and rear-delt movement rather than a heavy lift.

exercises.name: Banded Face Pull
exercises.description: Pull a resistance band toward your face with your elbows high. A light rear-delt and shoulder-health movement you can do anywhere.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.description: Curl dumbbells while leaning back on an incline bench so your arms hang behind your torso. Stretches and emphasizes the long head of the biceps.

exercises.name: Bayesian Cable Curl
exercises.description: Curl a cable handle from behind your body, facing away from the stack. Keeps the biceps loaded in the stretched position.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Preacher Curl
exercises.description: Curl an EZ-bar with your upper arms braced on a preacher pad. Isolates the biceps, with extra emphasis on the short head.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Preacher Curl
exercises.description: Curl one dumbbell at a time with your upper arm braced on a preacher pad. Isolates the biceps, especially the short head.

exercises.name: Standing Barbell Curl
exercises.description: Curl a straight barbell toward your shoulders while standing. A classic, heavy-loading biceps builder.

exercises.name: Standing EZ-Bar Curl
exercises.description: Curl an EZ-bar toward your shoulders while standing. The angled grip is easier on the wrists than a straight bar.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Curl
exercises.description: Sit on a bench and curl dumbbells toward your shoulders by bending your elbows. Isolates the biceps without leg or hip swing.
exercises.notes: Seated; the same curl standing is not a separate entry.

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Hammer Curl
exercises.description: Curl dumbbells with a neutral, thumbs-up grip. Targets the brachialis and brachioradialis for thicker upper arms and stronger forearms.
exercises.notes: Brachialis is counted under biceps; brachioradialis under forearms.

exercises.name: Cable Rope Hammer Curl
exercises.description: Curl a cable rope with a neutral grip. Keeps constant tension on the brachialis and brachioradialis.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Spider Curl
exercises.description: Lie chest-down on an incline bench and curl an EZ-bar with your arms hanging straight down. Strict biceps work with the short head emphasized.

exercises.name: Seated Concentration Curl
exercises.description: Sit on a bench and curl a dumbbell with your elbow braced against your inner thigh. A strict, one-arm biceps isolation.

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip EZ-Bar Curl
exercises.description: Curl an EZ-bar with an overhand grip. Targets the brachioradialis and forearms, with help from the biceps.

exercises.name: Behind-the-Back Barbell Wrist Curl
exercises.description: Hold a barbell behind your back and curl your wrists upward. Isolates the forearm flexors and builds grip strength.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Wrist Extension
exercises.description: Rest your forearms on your thighs or a bench and lift dumbbells with an overhand grip by extending your wrists. Builds the forearm extensors.

exercises.name: Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
exercises.description: Extend a cable rope overhead by straightening your elbows. Stretches and emphasizes the long head of the triceps.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Overhead Extension
exercises.description: Lean back on an incline bench and extend a dumbbell overhead by straightening your elbows. Stretches and emphasizes the long head of the triceps.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Skullcrusher
exercises.description: Lie on a bench and lower an EZ-bar toward your forehead, then extend your elbows. A heavy triceps isolation for all three heads.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Skullcrusher
exercises.description: Lie on a bench and lower dumbbells beside your head, then extend your elbows. A triceps isolation with a more natural wrist position.

exercises.name: Straight-Bar Cable Triceps Pushdown
exercises.description: Press a straight cable bar down by straightening your elbows. Loads the triceps heavily with constant tension.

exercises.name: Rope Cable Triceps Pushdown
exercises.description: Press a cable rope down and apart by straightening your elbows. Isolates the triceps, especially the lateral head, with constant tension.
exercises.notes: Rope version. A straight-bar pushdown is its own entry.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Cable Triceps Extension
exercises.description: Press a single cable handle down and across your body by straightening your elbow. Isolates each triceps one side at a time.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: Bench press with a narrower grip. Shifts the load toward the triceps while still working the chest and front delts.

exercises.name: Smith Machine JM Press
exercises.description: A hybrid of a close-grip press and a skullcrusher on a Smith machine. Heavy, guided triceps work.
exercises.notes: Hybrid movement; classified elbow-extension because the triceps are the target.

exercises.name: Barbell JM Press
exercises.description: A hybrid of a close-grip press and a skullcrusher: lower the bar toward your chin, then press up. Heavy triceps work.
exercises.notes: Hybrid movement; classified elbow-extension because the triceps are the target.

exercises.name: Weighted Triceps Dips
exercises.description: Dip between parallel bars with an upright torso, adding load with a dip belt. Emphasizes the triceps, with help from the chest.
exercises.notes: Upright torso. The forward-lean chest version is its own entry.

exercises.name: Diamond Push-Up
exercises.description: Push-up with your hands close together under your chest. A bodyweight triceps builder that also works the chest.

exercises.name: Barbell High-Bar Back Squat
exercises.description: Squat with a barbell resting across your upper back. A foundational lower-body strength builder for the quads and glutes.
exercises.notes: Heavy axial loading. High-bar position; a low-bar variant would be its own entry.

exercises.name: Barbell Front Squat
exercises.description: Squat with a barbell held across the front of your shoulders. The upright torso shifts work to the quads and demands core and upper-back strength.

exercises.name: Machine Hack Squat
exercises.description: Squat on an angled machine with your back against the pad. Emphasizes the quads along a fixed, stable path.
exercises.notes: Machine angle and path vary by manufacturer; treated as one entry in v1.

exercises.name: Pendulum Squat
exercises.description: Squat on a machine that swings you along an arc. Hammers the quads with a deep, stable, low-stress path.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
exercises.description: Squat with a bar that moves on fixed rails. A guided way to load the quads and glutes with a lot of stability.

exercises.name: 45-Degree Leg Press
exercises.description: Press a weighted sled away with your legs while seated. Builds the quads and glutes with a supported back and an easy-to-adjust load.
exercises.notes: Foot position changes emphasis. Primary substitution pair with hack-squat.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Press
exercises.description: Press the sled away with one leg at a time. Builds the quads and glutes while exposing and fixing side-to-side differences.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.description: Single-leg squat with your rear foot raised on a bench, holding dumbbells. Builds the quads and glutes and challenges balance.
exercises.notes: Loading is limited by grip and balance.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Walking Lunge
exercises.description: Step forward into a lunge with dumbbells in your hands, alternating legs as you walk. Builds the quads and glutes and challenges balance.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
exercises.description: Step backward into a lunge with dumbbells in your hands. Trains the quads and glutes with less stress on the front knee.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Step-Up
exercises.description: Step onto a box with dumbbells in your hands, driving through your front leg. Builds the quads and glutes one leg at a time.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Sissy Squat
exercises.description: Lean back and let your knees travel far forward as you lower, then rise. A demanding bodyweight quad isolation.
exercises.notes: A sissy squat bench or holding a support is optional; not listed as equipment.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Extension
exercises.description: Straighten your knees against a machine pad while seated. Isolates the quadriceps.
exercises.notes: Sissy squat is the closest isolation alternative; the compound quad exercises are weaker substitutes.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
exercises.description: Hold a dumbbell at your chest and squat. A beginner-friendly squat that trains the quads and core and teaches an upright torso.
exercises.notes: A kettlebell works the same way.

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: Lower a barbell along your legs by pushing your hips back, then stand tall. Trains the hamstrings and glutes with a long stretch.
exercises.notes: Hip hinge with soft knees; the bar stays close to the legs.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: Lower dumbbells along your legs by pushing your hips back, then stand tall. Trains the hamstrings and glutes with a long stretch.

exercises.name: Conventional Barbell Deadlift
exercises.description: Lift a barbell from the floor to standing by driving through your legs and hips. A heavy, full-body strength movement.
exercises.notes: High technique and recovery demand. Sumo and trap-bar versions are their own entries.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
exercises.description: Lift a trap bar from the floor while standing inside it. A heavy, back-friendly deadlift that blends squat and hinge.
exercises.notes: A squat-hinge hybrid; classified hinge.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
exercises.description: Lift a barbell from the floor with a wide stance and a more upright torso. A heavy lift for the glutes, hamstrings and inner thighs.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.description: Curl a machine pad toward you by bending your knees while seated. Isolates the hamstrings.
exercises.notes: Seated variant; the lying leg curl is its own entry.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.description: Lie face down and curl a machine pad toward your glutes by bending your knees. Isolates the hamstrings.

exercises.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
exercises.description: Kneel with your feet anchored and lower your torso forward as slowly as you can. A very demanding bodyweight hamstring exercise.
exercises.notes: A Nordic bench or any secure foot anchor works.

exercises.name: Swiss Ball Leg Curl
exercises.description: Lie on your back with your heels on a Swiss ball, lift your hips and roll the ball toward you. Trains the hamstrings and glutes with core control.

exercises.name: 45-Degree Hyperextension
exercises.description: Hinge at the hips over an angled bench and rise back up. Trains the hamstrings, glutes and lower back.
exercises.notes: Holding a plate adds load. Rounding the upper back shifts more work to the lower back.

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.description: Drive a barbell upward with your upper back resting on a bench. Directly targets the glutes through strong hip extension.
exercises.notes: Classified as hinge (hip extension).

exercises.name: Single-Leg Dumbbell Hip Thrust
exercises.description: Thrust a dumbbell upward on one leg with your upper back on a bench. Isolates each glute and exposes side-to-side differences.
exercises.notes: Classified as hinge (hip extension), like the barbell hip thrust.

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
exercises.description: Face away from a low cable and hinge your hips back, then drive them forward. Teaches the hip hinge and trains the glutes and hamstrings.

exercises.name: Cable Glute Kickback
exercises.description: With an ankle strap on a low cable, kick one leg straight back. Isolates the glutes through hip extension.
exercises.notes: Classified as hinge (hip extension).

exercises.name: Seated Machine Hip Abduction
exercises.description: Press your knees outward against the machine pads from a seated position. Isolates the glute medius and minimus.
exercises.notes: Glute medius and minimus are counted under glutes.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Hip Abduction
exercises.description: Sit on a bench with an ankle strap on a low cable and push your leg out to the side. Isolates the glute medius one side at a time.
exercises.notes: Glute medius is counted under glutes.

exercises.name: Standing Machine Calf Raise
exercises.description: Rise onto your toes under load, then lower under control. Isolates the calves.
exercises.notes: Straight knees, so the gastrocnemius does most of the work.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Standing Calf Raise
exercises.description: Rise onto your toes under a Smith machine bar with your toes on a block, then lower slowly. Isolates the calves with a stable setup.
exercises.notes: A calf block or plate under the toes gives the full stretch; not listed as equipment.

exercises.name: Leg Press Calf Press
exercises.description: Press the sled with just the balls of your feet on the platform. Isolates the calves with a supported back and easy loading.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Dumbbell Calf Raise
exercises.description: Rise onto the toes of one foot on a block while holding a dumbbell, then lower slowly. Trains each calf with a full stretch.
exercises.notes: A calf block or step under the toes gives the full stretch; not listed as equipment.

exercises.name: Seated Machine Calf Raise
exercises.description: Sit with your knees bent under the pad and rise onto your toes. The bent knee shifts the work to the soleus.
exercises.notes: Bent knees, so the soleus does more of the work than in standing raises.

exercises.name: Tibialis Anterior Raise
exercises.description: Lean against a wall and lift your toes toward your shins. Strengthens the muscle on the front of the lower leg.
exercises.notes: A tib bar adds load; not listed as equipment. No curated alternatives.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.description: Hang from a bar and raise your legs in front of you by curling your pelvis up. Works the abs and hip flexors.

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
exercises.description: Hang from a bar or brace on a captain's chair and raise your knees toward your chest. An easier hanging ab exercise.

exercises.name: Kneeling Cable Crunch
exercises.description: Kneel at a cable and curl your ribs toward your hips. Isolates the abs with adjustable resistance.
exercises.notes: No curated alternatives in v1.

exercises.name: Decline Bench Weighted Crunch
exercises.description: Lie on a decline bench holding a weight plate at your chest and curl your torso up. Loads the abs through a full range.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.description: Roll an ab wheel forward from your knees and pull back, keeping your torso rigid. A tough anti-extension exercise for the abs and core.

exercises.name: Seated Machine Ab Crunch
exercises.description: Sit in the machine and curl your torso forward against the pad. Isolates the abs with adjustable resistance.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Woodchopper
exercises.description: Rotate your torso to pull a cable diagonally across your body. Trains the obliques and core to rotate with control.

exercises.name: Weighted Russian Twist
exercises.description: Sit leaning back and rotate a weight plate from side to side. Works the obliques and core.

exercises.name: Standing Pallof Press
exercises.description: Press a cable or band straight out from your chest and hold while resisting the pull to rotate. A core anti-rotation exercise.
exercises.notes: Works with a resistance band as well as a cable.

exercises.name: RKC Plank
exercises.description: Hold a plank while squeezing your glutes, quads and abs as hard as you can. A short, intense hold that trains full-body tension.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Side Plank
exercises.description: Hold your body straight on one forearm and the side of one foot. Trains the obliques and the deep muscles beside the spine.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Dead Bug
exercises.description: Lie on your back and lower opposite arm and leg while keeping your lower back flat. Teaches core control and bracing.
